stem:
$\mathbf{Z}$ is a molecule which contains the elements carbon, hydrogen and oxygen only.

$\mathbf{Z}$ contains only alkene and carboxyl functional groups.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Complete Table 6.1 by describing the observations that occur when two different reagents are added to separate samples of $\mathbf{Z}\text{(aq)}$.

Table 6.1

| reagent added to $\mathbf{Z}\text{(aq)}$ | observation |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{Br}_2\text{(aq)}$ |  |
| $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\text{(s)}$ |  |

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Table 6.2 shows the percentage by mass of each element present in $\mathbf{Z}$.

Table 6.2

| element | percentage by mass / % |
| :--- | :--- |
| carbon | 41.38 |
| hydrogen | 3.45 |
| oxygen | 55.17 |

Using the data in Table 6.2, demonstrate that the empirical formula of $\mathbf{Z}$ is $\text{CHO}$. Show your working.

parts.label: (c)
(c)(i)
parts.text: Deduce the molecular formula of $\mathbf{Z}$. Explain your answer by referring to the molecular ion peak in Fig. 6.1 and the empirical formula of $\mathbf{Z}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Use Fig. 6.1 to suggest the formulae of the fragments with $m/e$ peaks at 45 and at 71.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Suggest the structure of $\mathbf{Z}$ using relevant information from Table 6.1, **(b)** and **(c)**.
